headline: Local Pharmacy Refuses To Dispense Aspirin To Former Head Of State Without Three Signed Permits From The Judiciary
body:
The local neighborhood pharmacy has officially denied a high-profile former politician a single tablet of aspirin, citing a rigid interpretation of a new judicial circular that requires all medical requests from former leaders to be processed through a triple-signature validation system. Pharmacist Ramesh Gupta insisted that even a basic headache requires an order from the Supreme Court, ensuring that the former leader’s recovery is as procedurally sound as a constitutional amendment.

“I have the aspirin right here behind the counter, but the court said it’s a security matter,” said Gupta, while checking a stack of stamped affidavits. “If I just hand over a strip of pain relief, how do I know it won’t destabilize the national morale? We have to treat this cough drop request with the same gravity as a multi-year land dispute. He is currently waiting in the queue behind a man buying cough syrup, but I’ve told him the man with the prescription gets precedence under the new 'Statutory Waiting' guidelines.”

Legal observers noted that the former prime minister’s symptoms are currently being handled by a special bench tasked with determining if a fever qualifies as an act of political defiance. The pharmacy has agreed to keep the medicine in a climate-controlled locker until the Chief Justice issues a formal directive on whether paracetamol can be administered without a hearing. In the meantime, the former leader has been advised to simply meditate on the stability of the state until the paperwork is processed.
caption: When a pharmacy requires a supreme court hearing to sell you a Crocin, you know you're living in peak bureaucracy. Has your local chemist ever asked for a writ petition for a band-aid? #Bureaucracy #HealthCare #JudicialHumor (satire)
